newsitem.title: THAILAND: RESEARCH ALERT-Thai risks overblown-Pacific Asset.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Thai risks overblown-Pacific Asset.

text.p: Despite anticipated slower economic growth and continued problems with the banking and property sectors, risks in Thailand have been blown out of proportion, Pacific Asset Management said on Monday.

The Singapore-based firm, which still recommended investors buy baht-denominated paper, said the recent massive cut in government spending should help address Thailand's current account deficit and ease pressure on baht, it said.

The Thai government, in a move to narrow the country's wide current account deficit, recently announced cuts of 99 billion baht (US$3.8 billion) in spending for the 1996/97 (October-September) financial year.
"Today, at least markets know that if a devaluation comes, it will be forced from the outside," the report said.
The company recommended investors buy baht-denominated papers at the 6-12 month tenor and hedge the exposure through the baht basket of currencies.

"We see no evidence of a shift in the basket weights and doubt whether the Bank of Thailand would find a larger weight for the yen appealing at today's level of nearly 125 per dollar," the report said.

"Finally, if investors hold the view that dollar strength (yen weakness) has now run its course, they may wish to reflect this in their baht investments by leaving the yen component of the basket out of the hedge," it said.
